# Jira Credential Setup¶

This guide walks you through setting up API token credentials for Jira in Jentic One using **Basic Auth** with a standard API token (no scopes).

## Overview¶

### What you'll need¶

- A Jira Cloud account (free tier available)
- Access to [Atlassian Account API Tokens](https://id.atlassian.com/manage/api-tokens)

### What you'll do¶

1. **Find Jira** in the Jentic Public API Catalog
2. **Create an API token** in your Atlassian account using the **"Create API token"** button (not "Create API token with scopes")
3. **Add a Basic Auth credential** for Jira using your email and API token, which includes it in your workspace
4. **Verify the connection** to ensure everything is working

> **Note:** This guide uses the standard **"Create API token"** button which creates a token without scopes. If you see an option for "Create API token with scopes", do not use that — use the regular "Create API token" button instead.

### Account Requirements¶

- **Free tier:** Jira Cloud free plan provides API access (up to 10 users, 2GB storage)
- **API tokens:** Tied to individual user accounts
- **Service accounts:** 5 free per organization; more than 5 requires Atlassian Guard subscription
- **Team credentials:** API tokens are per-user. Each team member creates their own token. For shared integrations, create a dedicated service account (service accounts must be licensed Jira users)

---

## Step-by-Step Instructions¶

### 1. Find Jira in the Jentic Public API Catalog¶

1. In the Jentic One UI, open the **Jentic Public API Catalog** and search for "Jira"
2. Select Jira and click **Add credential**
3. Adding a credential includes Jira in your workspace
4. Keep this tab open — you'll need to enter your credentials here

### 2. Create an API Token in Atlassian¶

1. Open a new tab and go to [Atlassian Account API Tokens](https://id.atlassian.com/manage/api-tokens)
2. Log in with your Atlassian account (the same account you use for Jira)
3. Click **Create API token** (not "Create API token with scopes")
4. This creates a standard API token without scopes, which is what you need for Basic Auth
5. Give the token a descriptive name (e.g., "Jentic Integration")
6. Set an expiration date (default: 1 year, configurable)
7. Click **Create**
8. **Copy the token immediately** — it's shown only once and cannot be retrieved later

> **Security tip:** Save your API token in a secure password manager. You'll need it to add credentials in Jentic One, and you may want to reuse it for other Atlassian products.

### 3. Add Basic Auth Credentials in Jentic One¶

1. In the Jentic One UI (where you clicked "Add credential" in Step 1), you'll see fields for Basic Auth:
2. **Your Atlassian domain:** Enter your Atlassian domain (just the domain part, not the full URL)
   - For example, if your Jira URL is `https://test.atlassian.net`, enter just `test`
   - The full format is `https://{your-domain}.atlassian.net`, so you only need to enter the `{your-domain}` part
3. **Username:** Enter your Atlassian account email address (the email you use to log into Jira)
4. **Password/Token:** Paste the API token you created in Step 2
5. Give your credential a descriptive name (e.g., "Jira API Token")
6. Click **Save** or **Connect** to complete the setup

> **Note:** For Basic Auth with Jira, you need to provide your Atlassian domain, your email address as the username, and your API token as the password. Jentic One will use these credentials to authenticate API requests to Jira.

### 4. Verify Setup¶

If no errors occurred, Jira should now be available in your **workspace** with credentials configured.

---

## Authentication Methods¶

Jira supports two authentication methods:

### API Token (Basic Auth) - Covered in this guide¶

- **What it is:** Email address + API token combination
- **Best for:** Most use cases, simple setup
- **Shared credentials:** Same token works across all Atlassian Cloud products
- **Important:** Use the **"Create API token"** button (without scopes) — do not use "Create API token with scopes" for this guide

### OAuth 2.0¶

- **What it is:** Token-based authentication managed by OAuth flow
- **Best for:** Applications requiring user consent and token refresh
- **Setup:** More complex, requires OAuth app registration in Atlassian

This guide covers **API Token (Basic Auth)** setup.

---

## Rate Limits & Token Management¶

- **Rate limits:** Varies by endpoint — typically 100 requests per minute
- **Token expiry:** Configurable when creating the token
- **Token security:** Treat API tokens like passwords. If compromised, revoke immediately and create a new one
- **Revoking tokens:** Go to [Atlassian Account API Tokens](https://id.atlassian.com/manage/api-tokens) to revoke or manage existing tokens

---

## Troubleshooting¶

### "Unauthorized" or "Authentication failed" error¶

**Possible causes and solutions:**

1. **Incorrect Atlassian domain**
2. Verify your domain is correct (just the domain part, e.g., `test` for `test.atlassian.net`)
3. Make sure you didn't include `.atlassian.net` in the domain field
4. **Email mismatch**
5. Verify your email address matches your Atlassian account email exactly
6. Check for typos or extra spaces
7. **API token issues**
8. Ensure you copied the API token correctly (no extra spaces before or after)
9. Check that the API token hasn't expired or been revoked
10. Go to [Atlassian Account API Tokens](https://id.atlassian.com/manage/api-tokens) to verify your token is still active

### "Rate limit exceeded" error¶

**What it means:** Jira has rate limits (typically 100 requests per minute per user)

**Solutions:**

1. **Wait before retrying**
2. Wait a few minutes before retrying your request
3. Rate limits reset after a short period
4. **Implement throttling**
5. Consider implementing request throttling in your integration
6. Reduce the frequency of API calls if possible

### "Token not found" error¶

**What it means:** The API token you're trying to use doesn't exist or can't be found

**Solutions:**

1. **Create a new token**
2. API tokens are shown only once when created — if you didn't save it, you'll need to create a new one
3. Go to [Atlassian Account API Tokens](https://id.atlassian.com/manage/api-tokens) to create a new token
4. **Verify account**
5. Make sure you're using the token associated with the correct Atlassian account
6. Ensure the token was created for the same account you're using in Jentic One

### Can't access Jira data¶

**Possible causes and solutions:**

1. **Account access**
2. Ensure your Atlassian account has access to the Jira instance you're trying to connect to
3. Verify you're using the correct Atlassian account (the one with Jira access)
4. **Permissions**
5. Verify your account has the necessary permissions in Jira
6. Check with your Jira administrator if you need additional permissions
7. **Instance URL**
8. Check that you're using the correct Jira Cloud instance URL if required
9. Verify the domain matches your Jira instance

---

## Next Steps¶

After setting up your Jira credentials:

- Use Jira in your self-hosted [Jentic One](https://github.com/jentic/jentic-one)
- Explore other Atlassian APIs using the same credentials
- Set up service accounts for team-wide integrations (requires Atlassian Guard for more than 5 service accounts)

---
